blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation. The task requires retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, binding entities and relations, and composing one coherent final image from multiple references. LongBanana contains 90 carefully designed tasks organized by a 3-by-3 taxonomy; each task includes about 32 reference images, 20 constraints, and 50 evaluation items, yielding 4,670 expert-specified atomic evaluation items in total. Its graph-grounded evaluation design instantiates each task with reference images and an entity-relation graph, then converts node, edge, and whole-graph obligations into checklist items for Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction. Reviewed expert labels include a 15% double-labeled subset with 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa. We further introduce LongBanana-Gen, an agent-harness framework for long-horizon image generation; experiments show that minimal agent harnesses improve over direct generation, while a ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect (RPR) workflow yields harness-dependent gains by strengthening evidence grounding and repair. Together, LongBanana provides an auditable testbed for measuring dense visual evidence use and a shared target for developing stronger agent-driven image-generation systems. Code and data are available at the project page: https://long-banana.com/.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍了Long Banana, 据我们所知,这是在代理驱动图像生成时代,第一个由专家设计并经过专家验证的长文多参考图像合成基准。 这项任务需要检索分散的视觉证据,拒绝分散注意力者,约束实体和关系,并从多个参考物中编织一个连贯的最终图像. Long Banana包含由3乘3分类法精心设计的90项任务;每项任务包括大约32个参考图像,20个限制,以及50个评价项目,总共产生4,670个专家指定的原子评价项目. 其以图表为基础的评价设计将每个任务与参考图像和实体关系图一起进行即时分析,然后将节点、边缘和全图义务转换成内容Fidelity、关系约束和全球约束满意度清单项目。 经审查的专家标签包括一个15%的双标签子集,准确协议为89.4%和0.83四方加权卡帕. 我们进一步引入了长视图像生成的代理harness框架LongBanana-Gen;实验显示,最小的代理电源比直接电源改进,而ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect(RPR)工作流程通过加强证据地面和修复而产生依赖电源的收益。 LongBanana公司共同提供了一个可审计的测试台,用于测量密集的视觉证据使用情况,以及开发更强大的代理驱动图像生成系统的共同目标。 项目网页上有代码和数据:https://long-banana.com/。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: A useful image-generation system [ 36 , 16 , 4 , 6 ] should be able to synthesize a new image from the visual evidence provided by the user, even when that evidence is spread across many references. Consider an accessories retailer preparing an advertisement for all handbags with dual parallel top handles ( Figure 1 ). The system must inspect a large inventory, select the relevant bags, reject visually similar distractors, preserve appearance details, and arrange the selected items according to the requested composition. The output may look realistic while still being wrong: it may use the wrong handbag, bind a handle style to the wrong object, violate a count or layout constraint, or introduce unsupported details. The central capability is therefore not visual plausibility alone, but reference-grounded synthesis across retrieval, rejection, binding, and composition.
blocks.zh: 一个有用的图像生成系统[36、16、4、6]应当能够从用户提供的视觉证据中合成一个新的图像,即使这些证据分散在许多参考文献中。 考虑设立一个配件零售商,为所有手提包制作广告,并带有双重平行的顶端手柄(图1)。 系统必须检查大型库存,选择相关袋,拒绝视似相似的分光器,保存外观细节,并按照要求的构成安排所选物品. 输出可能看起来既现实又仍然错误:它可能使用错误的手提包,将一个手柄样式绑在错误的对象上,违反计数或布局限制,或者引入不支持的细节. 因此,中心能力不单是视觉上的合理性,而是在检索、拒绝、绑定和组成方面以参考为基础的综合。

blocks.en: Evaluating this capability raises a central question: how can we tell whether an image-generation system has synthesized a correct image from long, multi-reference visual context? The difficulty is not only that such tasks contain more images or longer prompts. The required evidence is distributed across references, entities, attributes, relations, hard negatives, unsupported-content rules, and intermediate decisions. Success can only be judged by checking whether the final image satisfies the reference-grounded obligations. A benchmark therefore needs dense multi-reference tasks and scoring that localizes errors rather than a holistic score.
blocks.zh: 评估这种能力提出了一个中心问题:我们如何确定一个图像生成系统是否从长期,多参考的视觉上下文合成了正确的图像? 困难不仅在于这些任务包含更多的图像或更长的提示. 所需证据分布在参考文献、实体、属性、关系、硬底片、不支持内容规则和中间裁决之间。 判断成功与否,只能通过检查最终图像是否满足了参照基准义务。 因此,一个基准需要密集的多参考任务,并得分将错误本地化而不是整体分数。

blocks.en: Figure 1: LongBanana task overview. (a) Each case pairs a heterogeneous reference set and structured synthesis prompt with the generated image under evaluation. (b) LongBanana -Eval converts graph-grounded checklist items into dimension-level scores and auditable evidence traces. The score labels Content, Relations, and Global denote Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction, respectively.
blocks.zh: 图1:长巴纳纳任务概述. (a) 每个案例都与评价中生成的图像对应一套不同的参考材料和结构化的综合提示。 (b) Long Banana - Eval 将以图表为基础的清单项目转换成尺寸分数和可审计证据痕迹。 分数标签分别是内容、关系和Global表示内容Fieldity、关系约束和全球约束性满意度。

blocks.en: Current image-generation benchmarks [ 14 , 29 ] capture important parts of this problem, but leave the full measurement target under-specified. Research on instruction-guided editing, personalization, and prompt following addresses local edits and textual requirements [ 10 , 56 , 14 , 45 , 51 , 2 ] . Recent multi-reference benchmarks move closer to reference-based synthesis [ 23 , 37 , 3 ] , and automatic evaluation methods support systematic assessment [ 39 , 53 , 47 ] . What remains difficult to measure is dense evidence use: whether the model selected the right references, rejected plausible distractors, attached attributes and relations to the correct entities, and avoided content that is unsupported by either the instruction or the references. A realistic image can pass a surface-level inspection while failing exactly these obligations.
blocks.zh: 目前的图像生成基准[14,29]抓住了这个问题的重要部分,但留下了完全的测量指标的规格不足. 研究指导性编辑,个性化,以及后续地址的本地编辑和文字要求[10,56,14,45,51,2]. 最近的多参考基准更接近基于参考的综合[23、37、3],自动评价方法支持系统评估[39、53、47]。 仍然难以衡量的是密集的证据使用:模型是否选择了正确的引用,否定了可能的分心者,附着的属性和与正确实体的关系,并避免了指令或引用所不支持的内容. 一个现实的形象可以在完全不履行这些义务的情况下通过表面检查。

blocks.en: These failures are typically provenance errors rather than rendering errors, where provenance is the source—a specific reference, or the instruction itself—to which each piece of generated content should be attributed: a system may render the right object category while copying appearance from the wrong reference, place the correct entities while violating their relation, or produce a polished composition that leaks a hard negative into the scene. To make such errors measurable, we model each task as an entity–relation graph . Its nodes are the entities, attributes, and text elements that must (or must not) appear; its edges are the spatial, interaction, ordering, and local-appearance relations that bind those entities; and its whole-graph constraints are scene-level obligations—layout, counts, temporal state, and reference selection—that no single node or edge captures. We refer to a node, an edge, or a whole-graph constraint as a graph unit . These three levels define the three graph-grounded scoring dimensions used throughout the paper: Content Fidelity (node level), Relational Binding (edge level), and Global Constraint Satisfaction (whole-graph level). We derive a checklist of atomic, visually verifiable items, each tied to one graph unit, to localize failures.
blocks.zh: 这些故障通常是出处错误,而不是出处错误,因为出处是每一块生成的内容都应归属的来源——一种具体的参考,或指示本身:一个系统可能在复制错误参考物的外观的同时使对象类别正确,在违反其关系时将正确的实体放置,或产生一种抛光的成分,将硬负数泄露到现场。 为了衡量这些错误,我们把每项任务模拟为实体关系图。 它的节点是必须(或必须)出现的实体、属性和文本要素;它的边缘是约束这些实体的空间、互动、秩序和本地出现关系;它的全图限制是场景一级的义务——显示、计数、时间状态和参考选择——没有单一的节点或边缘捕捉。 我们把节点、边缘或全图约束称为图表单位。 这三层界定了整个文件所用的三个以图表为基础的评分维度:内容Fidelity(节点级),关系约束(对接级)和全球约束满意度(整图级)。 我们得到一份原子、可视可核查的物项清单,每个清单都与一个图表单元相连,以将故障本地化。

blocks.en: To make this benchmark auditable at scale, we design LongBanana -Eval, a graph-grounded checklist evaluation pipeline whose scorer LongBananaEval acts as an agentic checklist judge (Section 3 ): rather than judging the final image with one undifferentiated score, it routes each checklist item to a rubric-guided critic, invokes deterministic tools—OCR, counting, layout, and identity checks—when an item benefits from an executable check, and records evidence traces for quality control and reproducibility. We validate this measurement target on a human-audited pool of 900 generated outputs with 46,700 reviewed checklist labels. An independently double-labeled subset of 7,005 labels (15%) reaches 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted κ \kappa , and these reviewed expert checklist scores serve as the reference standard against which we validate LongBananaEval .
blocks.zh: 为了使这一基准可以大规模审计,我们设计了LongBanana-Eval,一个以图表为基础的清单评估管道,其计分员LongBanana-Eval担任清单代理人(第3节):它不是用一个无差别的分数来判断最后图像,而是将每个清单项目引向一个有指导意义的批评者,在某一项目受益于可执行的检查时,使用确定性工具——OCR、计数、布局和身份检查,并记录质量控制和可复制的证据痕迹。 我们验证了这一衡量指标,即由人审计的900项产出,并有46 700份经审查的核对清单标签。 由7,005个标签(15%)组成的独立双标签子集达到89.4%的准确协议和0.83个四重加权单位\kappa,这些经过审查的专家清单分数是我们验证LongBananaEval的参考标准。

blocks.en: We also use LongBanana to study agent-driven image-generation workflows. Each system wraps a fixed image generator in an agent harness [ 40 , 54 , 30 ] : the harness maintains reference state, selects evidence, schedules prompts, invokes the generator, and revises requests, while the image generator only synthesizes pixels. We evaluate direct generation, minimal agent harnesses, and RPR-enabled harnesses, where RPR is a serial workflow combining ReAct evidence grounding, Plan–Exec decomposition, and Reflect-based revision (Section 4 ), and we compare multiple image generators under a fixed harness. Across these settings, agent harnesses improve the aggregate profile over direct generation, yet no single harness dominates: the best per-subclass scores remain distributed across direct prompting, minimal harnesses, and RPR. RPR itself yields harness-dependent gains, helping only when the harness reliably exploits retrieved evidence and revision feedback, and otherwise introducing drift.
blocks.zh: 我们还利用LongBanana研究代理驱动的图像生成工作流程. 每个系统将一个固定的图像生成器包裹在一种代理电源中[40、54、30]: 控制带保持参考状态,选择证据,调度提示,引用生成器,并修改请求,而图像生成器只合成像素。 我们评价直接生成、最小的代理电源和RPR带动的电源,其中RPR是一个串联的工作流程,结合了ReAct证据地面、Plan-Exec分解和反射修正(第4节),我们比较了固定电源下的多个图像生成器。 通过这些环境,代理机在直接生成时会改善总体情况,然而没有单一的代理机能占据主导地位:每个子级的最佳分数仍然分布在直接触发、最小的牵引和RPR之间。 RPR本身产生依赖利用的效益,只有当这种利用可靠地利用了所收集的证据和修订反馈,或以其他方式引入漂移时才有所帮助。

blocks.en: • Benchmark setting and dataset. We introduce LongBanana -Bench for long-context multi-reference image synthesis, with 90 expert-designed cases, dense references, hard negatives, unsupported-content rules, and a 3 × 3 3\times 3 taxonomy. • Graph-grounded evaluation. We introduce LongBanana -Eval, mapping entity–relation graphs to atomic checklist items over Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction. • Expert verification and audit protocol. We provide reviewed expert checklist labels, agreement statistics, evidence traces, and scorer validation against human labels. • Agent-driven generation study. We evaluate direct, harness-based, and RPR workflows to show that current systems fail in structured, diagnosable ways rather than along a single image-quality axis.

blocks.en: 2 The LongBanana Benchmark
blocks.zh: 2 长巴纳纳基准

blocks.en: 2.1 Goal and Scope
blocks.zh: 2.1 目标和范围

blocks.en: LongBanana is an evaluation benchmark for long-horizon multi-reference image synthesis . A system is given a heterogeneous reference set and a structured synthesis instruction, and must render one coherent image that satisfies the obligations of the task’s entity–relation graph (Section 1 ): its required and forbidden nodes, the edges that bind them, and the whole-graph constraints on the scene. The setting differs from low-reference editing because the decisive evidence is distributed across many images, and correctness is measured by the graph-derived checklist of atomic, visually verifiable items rather than by a single holistic quality score. LongBanana contains 90 cases: 10 cases for each subclass in a 3 × 3 3\times 3 taxonomy. A typical case contains approximately 32 references and more than 20 cross-reference constraints, and across the benchmark experts specify 4,670 atomic checklist items. Because every item is tied to a single graph unit, each failure is localized to a specific obligation rather than absorbed into an overall score.
blocks.zh: Long Banana是长视多参考图像合成的评价基准。 一个系统被赋予了多样的参考集和结构化的综合指令,并且必须使一个一致的图像能够满足任务实体的义务 — — 关系图(第1节):它所要求的和被禁止的节点,绑定它们的边缘,以及现场的全图限制。 设定与低参考编辑不同,因为决定性证据分布在许多图像中,正确性由原子、可视化物品的图表清单而不是单一的整体质量分数来衡量。 Long Banana包含90个病例: 每个子类有10个病例,在一个3×3 3\times 3个分类. 一个典型案例包含大约32个参考和20多个相互参照的限制,跨基准专家指定了4 670个原子清单项目。 由于每件物品都与一个单一的图表单位相连,因此每件失败都被定位到特定的义务,而不是被吸收到一个整体的分数中.

blocks.en: Figure 2: The 3 × 3 3\times 3 taxonomy used to organize LongBanana . Rows group cases into Scene Composition, Visual Appearance, and Reference Reasoning, while columns expose subclass-level demands used for diagnostic reporting. Each subclass contributes 10 cases.
blocks.zh: 图2:用于组织Long Banana的3×3 3\Times 3分类法。 将病例分组为场景构成,视觉外观,以及参考理由,而列则暴露用于诊断报告的亚类要求. 每个子类贡献10个案例.

blocks.en: 2.2 Task Taxonomy and Evaluation Rubric
blocks.zh: 2.2 任务分类和评价

blocks.en: We organize LongBanana tasks into a three-suite taxonomy that captures their primary synthesis demands ( Figure 2 ). Across these tasks, a shared graph-grounded rubric evaluates whether the generated image preserves the required content, relations, and scene-level constraints.
blocks.zh: 我们把LongBanana的任务组织成一个三套组合的分类法,捕捉它们的主要合成需求(图2)。 在这些任务中,一个共享的图表定位标题评价生成的图像是否保留了所需的内容,关系和场景层面的限制.

blocks.en: The three suites are Scene Composition (semantic coverage, relational graph consistency, and layout arrangement), Visual Appearance (global appearance conditioning, local appearance binding, and appearance harmonization), and Reference Reasoning (selection and retrieval, temporal/state reasoning, and counting/aggregation). All tasks require a final image output; subclasses differ in the evidence-integration behavior being tested.
blocks.zh: 三个套房是场景构成(语义覆盖、关系图一致性和布局安排)、视觉外观(全球外观调节、局部外观约束和外观统一)和参考理由(选择和检索、时间/状态推理和计数/汇总)。 所有任务都需要最终的图像输出;子类在被测试的证据-整合行为上有所不同.

blocks.en: For each case, checklist items assess correctness at three levels of the entity–relation graph: nodes, edges, and the whole graph. Content Fidelity measures node-level correctness: required entities, attributes, text elements, and supported semantic nodes must appear, while forbidden or unsupported nodes must be absent. Relational Binding measures edge-level correctness, including spatial relations, interactions, ordering, support, containment, and local bindings such as texture, material, color, pose, or state assigned to a specific entity. Global Constraint Satisfaction measures whole-graph correctness, including composition, layout, scene-level style, count and aggregation constraints, temporal/state constraints, and reference-selection constraints.
blocks.zh: 对于每个案例,核对表项目在实体关系图的三个层次评估正确性:节点、边缘和整个图表。 内容 Fidelity 度量节点级别正确性:需要的实体,属性,文本元素,以及支持的语义节点必须出现,而禁止或不支持的节点必须缺失. 关系约束措施 边缘级正确性,包括空间关系,相互作用,订单,支持,封存,以及地方约束,如纹理,材料,颜色,姿势,或指定给特定实体的状态. 全球约束性满足度衡量全图正确性,包括组成,布局,场景级别风格,计数和汇总限制,时间/状态限制,以及参考选择限制.

blocks.en: This graph-grounded rubric localizes failures to specific content, bindings, or scene-level obligations, supporting consistent diagnosis across task categories and generation systems.
blocks.zh: 这个以图表为基础的标题将特定内容的失败、绑定或场景级义务本地化,支持跨任务类别和生成系统的一致诊断。

blocks.en: 2.3 Benchmark Construction
blocks.zh: 2.3 基准建设

blocks.en: We construct each case around a shared entity–relation graph that connects the synthesis instruction, reference images, and evaluation checklist ( Figure 3 ). Construction proceeds from a scenario description to structured constraints, then to the visual references and instruction that express the task, and finally to the checklist used to evaluate its result.
blocks.zh: 我们围绕一个共同的实体构建每个案例 — — 连接综合指令、参考图像和评价清单的关系图(图3)。 施工从情景描述到结构化制约,然后是表达任务的视觉参考和指示,最后是用来评估结果的核对表。

blocks.en: Expert authors design scenarios aligned with the task taxonomy, drawing on storyboard, product, and scene-composition use cases. A scenario specifies what the final image should depict and which entities, visual attributes, and interactions must be preserved. An LLM then structures the scenario into an entity–relation graph: nodes represent entities and their attributes, edges encode spatial relations, interactions, and local appearance bindings, and whole-graph constraints specify requirements such as composition and counts. This representation makes the dependencies explicit. For example, an appearance requirement identifies both the visual property and the entity to which it belongs, while a relational requirement identifies the entities that must participate in the requested configuration. These constraints guide both task synthesis and checklist derivation.
blocks.zh: 专家作者根据故事板、产品和场景组合使用案例设计符合任务分类的情景。 一种情景规定了最终图像应描绘什么,以及必须保留哪些实体、视觉属性和相互作用。 LLM然后将情景构建为实体-关系图:节点代表实体及其属性,边缘编码空间关系,相互作用,以及局部外观绑定,全图约束则指定了组成和计数等要求. 这种表述明确了依赖关系。 例如,外观要求既识别视觉属性,又识别其所属实体,而关系要求则识别必须参与所请求的配置的实体. 这些制约因素指导了任务综合和清单的制定。

blocks.en: The graph guides the creation of the target instruction and reference images, including entity, appearance, and optional background references. The instruction expresses the requested composition and the relationships to be realized; the references supply the visual identities, local details, and appearance cues needed to instantiate it. Discriminative visual attributes are retained in the references and omitted from text where possible. Because these cues are distributed across images, the generator must associate each relevant reference with the intended graph entity and combine their evidence while maintaining the requested relations. At least 30 cases also include two or more hard-negative references that are visually plausible but irrelevant to the requested output. Their exclusion is encoded in the checklist, allowing distractor leakage to be assessed alongside the inclusion of required content.
blocks.zh: 该图指导目标指令和参考图像的创建,包括实体,外观,以及可选背景参考. 该指示表达了所要求的组成和要实现的关系;参考文献提供了视觉身份、当地细节和显示该特征所需的外观提示。 在参考文献中保留了歧视性的视觉属性,并尽可能从文本中删除。 因为这些提示分布在图像之间,生成器必须将每个相关引用与预期的图体联系起来,并结合它们的证据,同时保持所要求的关系. 至少有30个案例还包括两个或两个以上的硬阴性参考文献,这些文献看起来是可信的,但与所要求的产出无关。 将其排除在外在清单中作了编码,允许在列入所需内容的同时评估分散干扰器泄漏情况。

blocks.en: We translate graph constraints into atomic checklist items using the rubric introduced in Section 2.2 . Node-level items check required entities and attributes; edge-level items check relations and appearance bindings; whole-graph items check scene-wide requirements such as layout and counts. Each item records an observable condition, the graph unit it evaluates, the relevant reference images, and its scoring criteria. This links a judgment about the output to the evidence needed to make it. Positive items test whether a required condition is satisfied, while negative items check for the absence of distractor or unsupported content. Each completed case therefore pairs an instruction and reference set with a checklist derived from the same task constraints. Section 3 describes how these items are scored.
blocks.zh: 我们使用第2.2节中引入的标题将图表限制转化为原子清单项目。 节点级项目检查所需的实体和属性;边缘级项目检查关系和外观绑定;全图项目检查布局和计数等全景要求. 每个项目记录一个可观测条件、它评价的图表单位、有关的参考图像及其评分标准。 这把对产出的判断与作出判断所需的证据联系起来。 阳性项目测试是否满足了所需的条件,而阴性项目则检查缺少分泌物或不支持的内容. 因此,每个已完成的案件都配有一套说明和参考,并配有来自相同任务限制的核对表。 第3节描述了这些项目如何得分。

blocks.en: Human curators review the instruction, reference images, and checklist together, checking their correspondence to the task graph. They inspect whether the references visibly support the required identities and attributes, whether the requested relations and composition are visually feasible, and whether checklist items express clear, individually verifiable conditions. They also check reference density, constraint coverage, and overlapping or ambiguous items. Requirements that cannot be judged from the references and a candidate output are revised or rejected before inclusion. Appendix B provides the detailed construction protocol and case specifications. Section 4 describes human labeling of generated outputs to establish reference judgments for evaluator validation.
blocks.zh: 人类馆长一起审查指示、参考图像和核对表,检查与任务图的对应情况。 它们检查参考文献是否明显支持所要求的身份和属性,所要求的关系和构成是否在视觉上可行,以及核对清单项目是否明确、可个别核查的条件。 它们还检查参考密度、限制范围以及重叠或模糊的项目。 无法从参考资料和候选人产出中判断的要求,在列入之前会予以订正或否决。 附 录 B提供了详细的施工规程和案例规格. 第4节说明人类对产出的标签,以建立参考判断,供评价人员验证。

blocks.en: Figure 3: LongBanana construction pipeline. (1) Scenario Construction : experts design scenarios aligned with the task taxonomy. (2) Graph Construction : an LLM structures each scenario into entities, attributes, relations, and whole-scene constraints. (3) Prompt & Reference Synthesis : the graph guides the creation of the target instruction and visual references. (4) Checklist & Curation : graph constraints are translated into evidence-linked checklist items, and human curators review the instruction, references, and checklist for consistency, visual feasibility, and verifiability.

blocks.en: LongBanana -Eval evaluates a generated image against the case’s graph-derived checklist. Its agentic checklist judge, LongBananaEval , prepares item-specific reference evidence, routes each check to a dimension-specific critic, and combines the resulting judgments into dimension-level and overall scores. As shown in Figure 4 , the pipeline also records the evidence supporting each item judgment.

blocks.en: The Content Fidelity critic checks required entities, attributes, and text, together with the absence of forbidden or distractor content. The Relational Binding critic checks spatial and interaction relations and the assignment of local appearance cues to their intended entities. The Global Constraint Satisfaction critic checks scene-wide requirements, including layout, global style, counts, and temporal or state constraints. Each critic compares the output with the item’s reference evidence and may invoke verification tools: OCR for readable text, detection or counting for multiplicity, layout routines for spatial constraints, and identity or feature matching for consistency. The critic combines these observations with the visual evidence to determine whether the item is satisfied.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: Our experiments connect evaluator validation with a study of long-context image generation. We first establish agreement between automatic checklist judgments and reviewed human labels. We then ask how much explicit graph structure helps a non-agentic generator, what adaptive agentic workflows add beyond an optimized static plan, and how those gains interact with the image backend.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验将评估鉴定与长文本图像生成的研究联系起来。 我们首先在自动核对表的判断和经过审查的人的标签之间达成协议。 然后,我们问,明确的图表结构对一个非代理生成器有多大帮助,在优化的静态计划之外增加了哪些适应性代理工作流程,这些收益如何与图像后端相互作用。

blocks.zh: 4.1 议定书和计量

blocks.en: We evaluate all systems on the held-out 90-case LongBanana benchmark. Table 2 fixes Nano Banana 2 and compares two direct baselines, three minimal agent harnesses, and their RPR-enabled variants. Table 3 fixes OpenClaw + RPR and compares three image backends. The shared OpenClaw + RPR with Nano Banana 2 configuration connects the two comparisons, yielding ten distinct generation conditions.

blocks.en: FP-Direct (full-prompt direct) keeps the full target prompt fixed and slides an eight-reference window over the inventory. PD-Direct (prompt-decomposed direct) tests how far non-agentic generation can go with explicit task structure and optimal composition scheduling. We give it privileged access to the entity–relation graph used to construct each case, including entity-to-reference correspondences. Under the same eight-reference backend budget as FP-Direct, it batches graph nodes and constructs relation-aware prompts. Its prompts expose relations incident to each batch, and each generated intermediate becomes the input for the next composition step. Integer programming solves the staging schedule exactly: first maximize relations whose anchors are composed no later than their dependents, then minimize total relational stretch ∑ ( u , v ) ∈ E | b ⁡ ( u ) − b ⁡ ( v ) | \sum_{(u,v)\in E}\lvert b(u)-b(v)\rvert , where b ⁡ ( ⋅ ) b(\cdot) is the batch index. blocks.en: The agentic conditions use Hermes-Agent, OpenCode, and OpenClaw, with Claude Sonnet 4.6 as their shared agent model. Output-level correlations establish closer alignment with expert score trends, while the item-level comparison shows improved decisions about individual requirements. These complementary results support using LongBananaEval to measure generation performance and produce evidence-linked diagnostic reports.
blocks.zh: 代理清单法官对所有三个产出层面的关联性措施达成了更高的一致。 在项目层面,它还将准确的ternary协议增加15.82个百分点,并将对面端的0~××××××××××××××××××××××2个错误减少19.28个百分点(表10). 产出层面的相互关系与专家的得分趋势更加一致,而项目层面的比较显示,对个别要求的决定有所改善。 这些补充成果支持使用LongBananaEval测量生成性能,并编制与证据相关的诊断报告。

blocks.en: 4.3 Generation Results and Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.3 生成结果和分析

blocks.en: Table 2: Harness and workflow comparison on the held-out 90-case LongBanana benchmark. The foundation image model is fixed to Nano Banana 2, and the compared component is the generation harness/workflow. Subclass columns and Overall Avg. report the unweighted checklist-average score (0–100); P@70% is the difficulty-weighted task pass rate. Higher is better for all reported metrics. Boldface and underlining mark the best and second-best values in each column.
blocks.zh: 表2:搁置的90个Long Banana基准的利用情况和工作流程比较。 基础图像模型固定在Nano Banana 2, 比较的组件是生成的牵引/工作流. 亚类列和Avery Avg.报告未加权的检查单平均分数(0–100);P@70%是难度加权任务通过率. 对所有报告的指标而言,更高的指标更好。 粗体字和下划线在每一栏标出最佳和次最佳值。

blocks.en: Table 2 establishes PD-Direct as a strong non-agentic baseline. Graph-informed staging substantially improves on FP-Direct, with the best Global Appearance Conditioning (GAC) score and the second-best Layout Arrangement Consistency (LAC) score across all compared systems. Its improvements also extend to local appearance binding, reference selection, and aggregation. These results demonstrate the practical value of exploiting known task structure: organizing entities and their relations into a precomputed composition schedule can support competitive multi-reference synthesis. The direct baseline remains competitive on these subclasses even against systems equipped with retrieval and reflection. PD-Direct’s strengths make the subsequent agentic comparison meaningful, since its task structure is supplied directly and its scheduling objective is solved exactly.
blocks.zh: 表2将PD-Direct确定为强有力的非代理基线。 以图示为基础的组合大大改进了FP-Direct,在所有比较的系统中,全球外观条件最佳得分和布局一致性第二最佳得分。 其改进范围还包括当地外观约束、参考选择和汇总。 这些结果显示了利用已知任务结构的实际价值:组织实体及其在预先计算的组成时间表中的关系可以支持竞争性的多参考综合。 在这些子类上,直接基线仍然具有竞争力,甚至对配备检索和反射的系统也是如此。 PD-Direct的长处使得随后的代理比较有意义,因为其任务结构是直接提供的,其调度目标也得到了准确的解决.

blocks.en: Agentic systems nevertheless achieve broader success without direct access to the construction graph. Most agentic configurations exceed PD-Direct in overall average, and OpenClaw + RPR surpasses it on eight of nine subclasses, with a 3.8-point average-score gain and a 12.2-percentage-point gain in task pass rate. This advantage reaches beyond scene composition to reference selection, state reasoning, and aggregation. The comparison exposes a gap between knowing the intended constraint structure and realizing it through successive image-generation steps. The graph specifies desired relations, while intermediate images reveal which constraints have actually survived the latest generation step. A fixed graph schedule organizes what should be composed; adaptive workflows can additionally inspect evidence, maintain reference bindings, and revise execution as synthesis unfolds. Their advantage over a structurally privileged baseline provides strong evidence for the value of agentic orchestration in long-context image generation.
blocks.zh: 然而,代理系统在没有直接查阅施工图的情况下取得了更广泛的成功。 多数代理配置在总体平均水平上超过了PD-Direct,OpenClaw+RPR在9个子类中的8个超过了它,平均得分增益3.8分,任务通过率增益12.2分. 这一优势超越了场景构成到参考选择,状态推理和汇总. 比较暴露了对预期制约结构的了解与通过连续生成图像的步骤实现这一结构之间的差距。 该图具体说明了希望建立的关系,而中间图像则显示哪些制约因素实际上在新一代的步骤中幸存下来。 固定的图表表安排了应当构成的内容;适应性工作流程可以额外检查证据,保持参考约束,并随着合成的展开修改执行. 它们相对于结构特权基线的优势提供了有力的证据,证明在长文本图像生成中,代理管弦法的价值。

blocks.en: Within the agentic configurations, RPR gives OpenClaw the strongest overall average and a joint-best task pass rate. Its clearest improvements over the minimal harness occur in scene composition, reference selection, and aggregation, consistent with a workflow that links evidence acquisition to execution and repair. The minimal OpenClaw harness remains stronger on temporal and state reasoning. OpenCode and Hermes-Agent also improve their average scores with RPR, while their task pass rates decline. These profiles identify reliable coordination as the next design priority: retrieved evidence must remain attached to the correct entities and constraints through planning, generation, and revision.
blocks.zh: 在代理配置中,RPR给予OpenClaw最强的总平均值和联合最佳任务通过率. 在现场组成、参考资料选择和汇总方面,与将证据获取与执行和维修联系起来的工作流程相一致,比最低限度的利用方式有了最明显的改进。 在时间和状态推理方面,OpenClaw的最低限度手段仍然更强大。 OpenCode和Hermes-Agent也用RPR提高了平均分数,同时任务通过率下降. 这些简介将可靠的协调确定为下一个设计优先事项:收集的证据必须始终附在正确的实体身上,并通过规划、生成和修订加以限制。

blocks.en: The RPR ablation in Table 11 isolates retrieval, planning, and reflection with OpenClaw and Nano Banana 2 fixed. Plan–Exec alone is strongest on global appearance conditioning and local appearance binding; ReAct alone improves reference selection over the minimal harness; and Reflect alone improves layout, aggregation, and task pass rate. The full workflow achieves the strongest overall result and pass rate among the component variants.
blocks.zh: 表11中的RPR扩张将检索、规划和反思与OpenClaw和Nano Banana 2固定在一起。 Plan-Exec 单是在全球外观条件和当地外观绑定上最强; ReAct 单是改进了参考选择,而不是最小的牵引; 单是反思可以改善布局,聚合,和任务通过率. 整个工作流程在各组成部分变量中实现最强的总体结果和通过率。

blocks.en: These profiles give a concrete direction for agent design. Evidence retrieval supplies the relevant references, planning organizes their use, and reflection checks the realized composition against the task. Their combined workflow turns these operations into a coordinated generation process, extending the benefits of decomposition with evidence inspection and feedback. The component results reinforce the main comparison: static organization is useful, and its integration with grounding and repair produces the strongest overall configuration in this study.
blocks.zh: 这些简介为剂剂设计提供了具体的方向. 证据检索提供了相关参考文献,计划安排其使用,反思对照任务检查实际构成。 它们的联合工作流程将这些行动转变为一个协调的生成过程,扩大了分解与证据检查和反馈的好处。 构成部分结果加强了主要比较:静态组织是有用的,它与地面和修理的结合产生了本研究中最强的整体配置.

The generation harness/workflow is fixed to OpenClaw + RPR, and the compared component is the foundation image model. Subclass columns and Overall Avg. use the same unweighted checklist-average score as Table 2 (0–100); P@70% is the difficulty-weighted task pass rate. Higher is better for all reported metrics. Boldface and underlining mark the best and second-best values in each column.
blocks.zh: 表3:与同一90例LongBanana基准的基金会图像模型比较。 生成牵引/工作流被固定为OpenClaw + RPR,比较的组件是基础图像模型. 亚类列和Avery Avg.使用与表2(0–100)相同的未加权清单平均分数;P@70%是难度加权任务通过率. 对所有报告的指标而言,更高的指标更好。 粗体字和下划线在每一栏标出最佳和次最佳值。

blocks.en: With OpenClaw + RPR fixed, Nano Banana 2 leads across all nine subclasses ( Table 3 ). Seedream 4 is stronger than GPT Image 1 on scene composition, temporal and state reasoning, and aggregation, whereas GPT Image 1 is more competitive on visual appearance and reference selection. The fixed workflow makes these differences informative about each backend’s ability to realize reference-grounded instructions.
blocks.zh: OpenClaw + RPR 固定后, 纳米香蕉 2 领先于所有9个子类(表3)。 种子梦4在场景组成,时间和状态推理以及聚合上比GPT图像1更强,而GPT图像1在视觉外观和参考选择上更具竞争力. 固定的工作流程使这些差异为每个后端实现基于参考的指示的能力提供信息。

blocks.en: Backend capability and agentic orchestration offer complementary paths to improvement. The harness controls evidence selection, constraint organization, and revision, while the image model determines how faithfully these decisions become pixels. A stronger workflow improves the use of the available visual evidence; a stronger backend improves its realization in the generated image. The broad Nano Banana 2 advantage shows that backend capability remains consequential even under the strongest evaluated workflow.
blocks.zh: 后端能力和代理管弦为改进提供了补充途径。 控制器控制了证据选择,约束组织,以及修订,而图像模型则决定这些决定是如何忠实地变成像素的. 更强大的工作流程可以改善现有视觉证据的使用;更强大的后端可以改善生成图像中的实现. 广泛的纳米香蕉2的优势表明,即使在最强的评价工作流程下,后端能力仍然会产生后果。

blocks.en: The comparison with PD-Direct highlights the distinction between planning a composition and controlling its realization. PD-Direct uses privileged graph information to optimize reference grouping and ordering, then executes that schedule in stages. The resulting images can still depart from the intended constraints as entities are added or edited. Agentic workflows can inspect intermediate outputs, revisit reference evidence, and adjust subsequent actions. Their broader advantage motivates treating the evolving visual state, alongside the task structure, as central to generation control.
blocks.zh: 与PD-Direct的比较突出了规划组成与控制其实现之间的区别. PD-Direct使用特权图信息来优化引用分组和顺序,然后分阶段执行该调度. 随着实体的加入或编辑,由此产生的图像仍然可以脱离预期的限制。 代理工作流程可以检查中间产出,重温参考证据,并调整后续行动. 它们更广泛的优势促使人们将不断变化的视觉状态与任务结构一起作为生成控制的核心。

blocks.en: The checklist turns this control problem into inspectable requirements. PD-Direct’s strong appearance conditioning alongside its weaker reference selection and state reasoning directs attention to evidence use across composition steps. Item judgments and evidence traces can distinguish an incorrect reference choice from an incorrect entity binding or an unmet scene-wide requirement. For future agent designs, these diagnostics offer a basis for choosing what to revisit and what to preserve during revision. The resulting research target is evidence-guided adaptation: connect inspection of the current image to the next retrieval, generation, or repair action while preserving satisfied constraints.
blocks.zh: 核对表将这一管制问题变成可检查的要求。 PD-Direct的强烈外观条件, 项目判断和证据痕迹可以区分错误的参考选择和不正确的约束实体或未满足的全场要求。 对于未来的剂剂设计,这些诊断为选择在修订过程中重新审视和保存什么提供了基础. 由此产生的研究目标是以证据为指南的适应:将当前图像的检查与下一个检索、生成或修复行动联系起来,同时保留令人满意的限制。

blocks.en: Appendix D reports the workflow ablation and case-paired score diagnostics. The generation comparisons, component study, and item-level traces together connect aggregate performance to the decisions made during synthesis, providing a basis for developing more capable reference-grounded image-generation agents.
blocks.zh: 附 录 D报告了工作流程减速和病例保值分析。 生成比较,组件研究,和项级的痕迹一起将聚合性能与合成过程中作出的决定联系起来,为开发更有能力的基于参考的图像生成剂提供了基础.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: LongBanana establishes long-context multi-reference image synthesis as a benchmark for integrating dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, and satisfying coupled content and relational constraints. LongBanana -Bench provides 90 expert-designed and expert-verified cases across a 3 × 3 3\times 3 taxonomy, with 4,670 atomic checklist items. LongBanana -Eval turns these constraints into evidence-linked judgments, validated against human labels, to measure constraint fulfillment and localize generation failures.
blocks.zh: LongBanana建立了长文本多参考图像合成,作为整合分散的视觉证据、拒绝分散注意力者以及满足内容和关系限制的基准。 Long Banana - Bench提供了90个专家设计并经过专家验证的病例,跨越3×3 3\times 3个分类,有4,670个原子清单项目. 龙巴纳纳 -Eval将这些限制转化为与证据相关的判断,用人类的标签加以验证,以衡量限制的实现情况,并使生成失败本地化。

blocks.en: The generation study highlights the distinction between optimizing a composition plan and adaptively controlling its realization. PD-Direct combines privileged access to the construction graph with exactly optimized staging, establishing a competitive non-agentic baseline. Agentic workflows achieve broader success without direct access to that graph, showing the value of adaptive evidence use and generation control beyond a fixed schedule. The RPR component study further supports coordinating retrieval, execution, and repair within one workflow. These findings point toward agents that reason over both task structure and the evolving visual state, preserve reference bindings across steps, and target unmet requirements during revision.
blocks.zh: 世代研究强调优化组成计划与适应性控制其实现之间的区别. PD-Direct将建筑图的特权获取与精确优化的中转相结合,建立了具有竞争力的非代理基线。 代理工作流程在无法直接访问该图表的情况下取得了更广泛的成功,显示了适应性证据使用和生成控制超过固定时间表的价值。 PR部分研究进一步支持在一个工作流程内协调检索、执行和修复。 这些调查结果指出,各种因素对任务结构和不断变化的视觉状态都具有理由,在各种步骤之间保留参考约束力,并针对修订过程中未达到的要求。

blocks.en: Image-generation benchmarks cover instruction-guided editing, personalization, human alignment, and reasoning-oriented synthesis [ 48 , 29 , 28 , 22 , 46 , 24 ] but generally focus on creating a single image from a single prompt. Recent multi-reference benchmarks [ 23 , 37 , 42 , 3 ] are closer to our setting, but they typically use fewer references or lower-density cross-image constraints. LongBanana targets final-image synthesis in which correctness depends on retrieving, rejecting, binding, and integrating evidence distributed across dozens of references.
blocks.zh: 图像生成基准包括指导性编辑,个性化,人配对,以及面向推理的合成[48,29,28,22,46,24],但一般侧重于从单一的提示创建单一图像. 最近的多参考基准[23、37、42、3]更接近于我们的设定,但它们通常使用较少的参考或密度较低的跨图像限制。 Long Banana针对的是最终图像合成,其中正确性取决于检索、拒绝、约束和整合分布在数十个参考文献中的证据。

blocks.en: Long-context tasks have long been a central challenge across language and vision domains [ 23 , 1 , 41 , 18 , 19 ] . Instruction-following benchmarks in NLP often convert open-ended tasks into verifiable atomic requirements. IFEval [ 55 ] emphasizes directly checkable constraints, and TIFA [ 11 ] converts text-to-image faithfulness into question-answer checks. LongBanana transfers this principle to long-horizon multi-reference synthesis. Each checklist item links the output to a graph node, graph edge, or whole-graph constraint, so failures can be traced to missing content, incorrect relations, hard-negative leakage, unsupported content, or global constraint violations.
blocks.zh: 长篇大论的任务长期以来一直是跨语言和愿景领域的中心挑战[23、1、41、18、19]。 NLP中遵循指令的基准,经常将开放式任务转化为可核查的原子要求. IFEval [55] 强调直接可核查的制约,TIFA [11] 将文本对图像的忠实性转换成问答检查. Long Banana将这一原则转移至长视多参考合成. 每个核对表项目将输出链接到一个图表节点,图边,或全图约束,因此失败可以追溯到内容缺失,关系不正确,硬负泄漏,内容不支持,或全球约束违反.

blocks.en: Low-level metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS [ 12 , 35 , 49 ] are poorly matched to reference faithfulness, motivating model-based judges and rubric evaluators [ 5 , 9 , 15 , 43 , 20 , 33 , 44 , 26 , 52 , 53 , 38 , 7 , 58 , 27 , 8 , 57 ] . However, a holistic judge can conflate realism with correctness when many references are present [ 21 , 32 , 34 , 50 , 17 ] . LongBananaEval evaluates checklist-level evidence with routed critics and tools, and we report its validity through Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall agreement with reviewed expert labels [ 31 , 25 , 13 ] .
blocks.zh: PSNR,SSIM,LPIPS[12,35,49]等低级度量衡与参考忠诚度不匹配,激励了以模型为基础的评委和评委[5,9,15,43,20,33,44,26,52,53,38,7,58,27,8,57]. 然而,当许多参考文献出现时,整体法官可以将现实主义与正确性混为一谈[21,32,34,50,17]. 龙巴纳纳 Eval用路由批评者和工具评价清单层面的证据,我们通过皮尔逊、斯皮尔曼和肯德尔与经过审查的专家标签的协议报告其有效性[31、25、13]。

blocks.en: A checklist item is valid only if it is visually verifiable, reference-grounded, and non-redundant where possible. Positive items evaluate whether a required fact is present and correctly bound. Negative items are Content Fidelity checks that evaluate whether a distractor or unsupported element is absent: completely absent is labeled 2, visually suspicious or ambiguous leakage is labeled 1, and full erroneous appearance is labeled 0. Items requiring specialist interpretation include a short reference note identifying the evidence to inspect.

blocks.en: Annotators view the reference set, target instruction, generated output, checklist item evidence, and explicit 0/1/2 scoring instructions. Human reviewers assign 46,700 reviewed checklist labels by applying all 4,670 benchmark checklist items to every reported condition. The three rubric dimensions are computed from the corresponding checklist labels. The protocol uses primary annotation, second-pass review, third-pass expert adjudication, an independently double-labeled subset of 7,005 labels, stratified audit sampling, schema validation, and score-stability checks. The annotation audit records include qualification and training criteria, review status, correction logs, adjudication logs, audit outcomes, and stability summaries without exposing annotator identities. blocks.en: FP-Direct uses the full target prompt throughout generation and varies only the visible reference window. Because a case may contain more reference images than the backend can consume at once, the implementation uses a window of eight references and iterates over the ordered reference inventory, e.g., ref1--ref8 , ref9--ref16 , and so on until all non-background references have been exposed. Each round receives the same complete target prompt; there is no entity-level batching, graph-conditioned relation filtering, explicit state memory, or repair step.
blocks.zh: FP-Direct使用整个生成时的全目标提示,并且只不同可见的参考窗口. 由于一个案例可能包含比后端能同时消耗的更多参考图像,因此执行使用8个参考窗口,并且对所订购的参考目录进行迭代,如ref1-ref8,ref9-ref16等,直到所有非背景参考都曝光. 每回合都得到相同的完整目标提示;没有实体级的批量,图形条件关系过滤,明确状态内存,或修复步骤.

blocks.en: PD-Direct is a deterministic staged-composition baseline rather than a free-form planning agent. It uses the same eight-reference backend budget as FP-Direct, but allocates that budget by graph structure rather than by inventory order. Each non-background entity node is represented by one reference image. Starting from the pre-generated background image, PD-Direct composes non-background entities in ordered batches of at most eight entity references, following the staging schedule that is optimal for the case’s entity–relation graph. Let b ⁡ ( v ) ∈ { 1 , … , K } b(v)\in\{1,\dots,K\} be the batch index of entity v v , with K = ⌈ N / 8 ⌉ K=\lceil N/8\rceil , at most eight entity references per batch, and the background fixed at batch 0 0 . Over the (unweighted, directed, possibly cyclic) entity–relation graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , the schedule minimizes a lexicographic objective: first the number of relations ( u , v ) (u,v) whose anchor is composed later than its dependent, | { ( u , v ) ∈ E : b ⁡ ( u ) > b ⁡ ( v ) } | \lvert\{(u,v)\in E:b(u)>b(v)\}\rvert , a capacity-constrained feedback-arc count that we minimize exactly by integer programming, and, among schedules attaining that minimum, the total relational stretch ∑ ( u , v ) ∈ E | b ⁡ ( u ) − b ⁡ ( v ) | \sum_{(u,v)\in E}\lvert b(u)-b(v)\rvert . We solve it exactly with an integer program (Pass 1 minimizes the feedback count F ⋆ F^{\star} ; Pass 2 minimizes the stretch subject to the feedback count equal to F ⋆ F^{\star} ); each case has a small number of composed entities ( N ≤ 32 N\leq 32 ), so the integer program solves in seconds. At step zero the backend receives the background image plus the first batch’s reference images and produces intermediate_00.png ; at each later step it receives the previous intermediate image plus the next batch’s references, and the final intermediate is saved as target/target_image.png . For a case with N = 32 N=32 composed entities this yields K = ⌈ N / 8 ⌉ = 4 K=\lceil N/8\rceil=4 batches and four intermediate images. The prompt at each step is constructed deterministically from fixed staged-composition instructions, the scene prompt, the entity types in the current batch, and all graph edges incident to that batch (there is no per-step cap on edges, so every relation is presented at the step of its later endpoint), followed by constraints to preserve existing content and maintain consistent lighting, scale, and perspective. Reference images and the background are generated upstream from the entity catalog, scene specification, and entity–relation graph; PD-Direct only stages their use during target construction.

blocks.en: The ablation shows that the three agentic stages are complementary rather than individually monotonic. Plan–Exec alone gives the strongest Visual Appearance scores on GAC and LAB, consistent with decomposition helping product, style, and material organization, but it weakens relation control and structured reasoning when evidence retrieval and repair are not coupled to the plan. ReAct alone improves selection relative to the minimal OpenClaw harness, but its overall score drops because evidence selection without explicit execution control does not reliably preserve spatial and appearance bindings through generation. Reflect alone raises LAC, AGG, and P@70%, indicating that revision helps repair visible layout and aggregation errors, but it can also over-correct or drift when missing evidence is not re-grounded.
blocks.zh: 衰减表明,三个剂态阶段是互补的,而不是单个单态的. Plan–Exec单独给出了GAC和LAB上最强的视觉外观分数,与分解帮助产品,风格和物质组织一致,但当证据检索和修复没有与计划结合时,它削弱了关系控制和结构化推理. 相对于最小的OpenClaw拉带而言,ReAct单独改进了选择,但其总得分下降,因为没有明确执行控制的证据选择并不能可靠地通过生成来保持空间和外观绑定. 单独反思提高LAC,AGG,和P@70%,表示修订有助于修复可见的布局和集合错误,但当缺失的证据没有重新定位时,它也可能过错或漂移.

blocks.en: The full RPR stack gives the best overall score and pass rate because the stages close each other’s failure modes: ReAct grounds the reference set, Plan–Exec turns the grounded state into an executable synthesis schedule, and Reflect supports revision based on the generated result. The remaining TSR drop relative to minimal OpenClaw suggests that temporal and state-reasoning cases are sensitive to over-revision: once a physically plausible final state is found, additional repair can shift pose or event timing away from the intended state. Thus, RPR is best interpreted as an evidence-preserving orchestration pattern, not as a uniformly beneficial amount of extra reasoning.
blocks.zh: 全RPR堆栈给出了最佳的整体得分和通过率,因为各个阶段相互关闭了失败模式: ReAct 为参考集提供依据, Plan–Exec 将被禁状态转换为可执行的合成时间表, 并基于生成结果支持修订 。 与最小的OpenClaw相比,其余的TSR下降表明,时间和状态下的案件对过度修正很敏感:一旦发现物理上可行的最终状态,额外的修复可以改变场景或事件时间,脱离预期状态. 因此,RPR最好被解释为一种保存证据的管弦图案,而不是一个统一有益的额外推理。

blocks.en: E.1 Limitations
blocks.zh: E.1 限制

blocks.en: The 3 × 3 3\times 3 taxonomy covers a meaningful subset of long-horizon multi-reference synthesis, but does not cover video generation, 3D scene composition, or unrestricted multimodal planning. The benchmark is intentionally high-density, which improves diagnostic resolution but makes expert annotation expensive. LongBananaEval depends on backbone multimodal models and verification tools, so model identifiers and tool versions must accompany final results.
blocks.zh: 3×3 3\times 3分类学涵盖一个有意义的子集长视多参考合成,但不涵盖视频生成,3D场景组成,或不受限制的多式联运规划. 基准是故意高密度的,这提高了诊断分辨率,但使专家的注解昂贵。 龙巴纳纳 Eval依赖于主干多式联运模型和验证工具,因此模型识别符和工具版本必须伴随最终结果.

blocks.en: E.2 Broader Impact Details
blocks.zh: E.2 更广泛的影响细节

blocks.en: The benchmark is designed for measurement rather than deployment, but it evaluates systems capable of generating realistic composite images from many references. Positive uses include model auditing and failure diagnosis. Risks include deceptive media, impersonation, privacy leakage, biased reference coverage, and copyright-sensitive reuse. Mitigations include filtering unsafe content, documenting provenance, restricting problematic assets, and providing a project issue tracker for reporting release problems at https://github.com/TIGER-AI-Lab/LongBanana/issues .
blocks.zh: 该基准旨在衡量而不是部署,但它评价能够从许多参考文献中生成现实综合图像的系统。 积极用途包括模式审计和失败诊断. 风险包括欺骗性媒体、冒充、隐私泄露、有偏见的参考报道和对版权敏感的再利用。 缓解措施包括过滤不安全内容,记录出处,限制有问题的资产,在https://github.com/TIGER-AI-Lab/LongBanana/issues上为报告发布问题提供项目问题跟踪器。

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and Section 1 state the benchmark, evaluator, and empirical claims, while Sections 2 , 3 , 4 and 5 define the scope and required evidence. Run-specific factual details are provided in the anonymized OpenReview artifacts and associated run records. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Appendix E discusses benchmark scope, annotation expense, and evaluator dependence. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not present theoretical theorems or formal proof claims. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [No] Justification: The paper describes benchmark construction, scoring, model and harness identifiers, and baseline implementations in Sections 2 , 3 , 4 , B , C and D , but does not include executable reproduction commands or environment files. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [No] Justification: This preprint does not provide a public data/code access link with executable reproduction instructions. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The experimental design, 90-case benchmark, evaluator configuration, metrics, and ablations are described in Sections 2 , 3 and 4 . Appendix C identifies the agent and judging models and the harness versions. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 4 reports checklist-average generation scores and the secondary difficulty-weighted P@70% diagnostic. Appendix D reports case-level bootstrap confidence intervals and paired tests for the checklist-average scores; judge–human agreement is reported as correlation diagnostics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [No] Justification: The paper identifies the generation and judging models but does not report per-run compute resources, runtime, or API costs. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Asset provenance and privacy screening are discussed in Appendix B ; broader impacts and responsible-release safeguards are discussed in Appendix E . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Appendix E discusses positive impacts for evaluation rigor and negative risks related to deceptive media, privacy, copyright, and biased coverage, together with mitigation measures. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Appendix B describes asset screening and redistribution restrictions; Appendix E describes responsible-release safeguards and takedown/contact procedures. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Asset provenance and licensing are documented in Sections 2 and B , covering source images, models, tools, and external benchmarks. Source citations, license/TOS audit results, and redistribution decisions are included in the submitted artifact metadata. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The benchmark, manifests, annotation schema, scorer configuration, and documentation are described in Sections 2 , 3 , B and C . The dataset card, manifest, release license, and anonymized artifact access information are provided in the submitted OpenReview artifacts. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The annotation workflow, adjudication plan, compensation reporting, and instruction/screenshot requirements are described in Sections 2 and B . Instructions, UI screenshots, rater counts, qualification criteria, compensation rate, and annotation time are reported as annotation metadata. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Participant-risk and review-status reporting are specified in Appendices B and E while preserving submission anonymity. The IRB exemption or equivalent review status is reported in anonymized form where applicable. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: LLM and MLLM usage in generation harnesses, rubric critics, tool routing, and evidence analysis is described in Sections 3 and C . The appendix reports the shared underlying agent model for generation harnesses, harness versions, and the Gemini 3 Flash judging backbone used by both the agentic checklist judge and the single-pass VLM judge. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 该摘要和第1节阐述了基准、评估者和经验性索赔,而第2、3、4和5节界定了范围和所需证据。 匿名开放审查文物和相关运行记录中提供了具体运行的事实细节。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由:附录 E讨论了基准范围、注释费用和评价者的依赖性。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文不提出理论定理或正式证明主张. 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:理由: 文件在第2、第3、第4、第B、第C和第D节中描述了基准构建、评分、模型和使用标识符以及基线执行情况,但不包括可执行的复制命令或环境文件。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:理由: 此预印不提供带有可执行复制指令的公共数据/代码访问链接. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 第2、第3和第4节介绍了实验设计、90项基准、评价者配置、衡量尺度和模拟。 附 录 C 识别代理,判断模型和机身版本. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明:第4节报告清单-平均生成分数和二级难度加权P@70%诊断。 附 录 D报告案例级的靴子置信间隔和核对表平均分数的配对测试;法官-人类同意作为相关诊断报告。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:理由: 文件确定了生成和判断模型,但没有报告每个运行的计算资源、运行时间或API成本。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是] 附录B讨论了资产来源和隐私筛选;附录E讨论了更广泛的影响和负责任的释放保障。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由:附录 E讨论了与欺骗媒体、隐私、版权和有偏见的报道有关的评价严格度的积极影响和负面风险,以及缓解措施。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[是] 理由:附录 B描述了资产筛选和再分配限制;附录E描述了负责任的释放保障和取走/接触程序。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 第2和B节记录了资产来源和许可证发放情况,包括来源图像、模型、工具和外部基准。 提交的人工元数据包括来源引用、许可证/技术选择系统审计结果和再分配决定。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[是] 第2、3、B和C节介绍了基准、清单、注释计划、记分器配置和文件。 所提交的公开审查文物中提供数据集卡、清单、发放许可证和匿名文物访问信息。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 第2节和B节介绍了注释工作流程、裁定计划、报酬报告和指示/截图要求。 指令,UI截图,评分计数,资格标准,补偿率,注释时间作为注释元数据报告. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[是] 理由说明:附录B和E规定了参与风险和审查状况报告,同时保留了提交的匿名性。 移民和难民委员会的豁免或同等审查状况酌情以匿名形式报告。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[是] 说明:LLM和MLLM在生成带、批判器、工具路由和证据分析中的使用情况载于第3和C节。 附录报告了通用的基本剂型号,用于发电机、机床版本和双子座3 Flash判断主干,该主干由代理清单法官和单传VLM法官使用。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The abstract and Section 1 state the benchmark, evaluator, and empirical claims, while Sections 2 , 3 , 4 and 5 define the scope and required evidence. Run-specific factual details are provided in the anonymized OpenReview artifacts and associated run records.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 该摘要和第1节阐述了基准、评估者和经验性索赔,而第2、3、4和5节界定了范围和所需证据。 匿名开放审查文物和相关运行记录中提供了具体运行的事实细节。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。
